intro.text: Smith+Nephew is a portfolio medical technology business focused on the repair, regeneration and replacement of soft and hard tissue. We exist to restore people’s bodies and their self-belief by using technology to take the limits off living. We call this purpose ‘Life Unlimited’. Our 17,000 employees deliver this mission every day, making a difference to patients’ lives through the excellence of our product portfolio, and the invention and application of new technologies across our three global business units of Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT and Advanced Wound Management. Founded in Hull, UK, in 1856, we now operate in around 100 countries, and generated annual sales of $6.2 billion in 2025. Smith+Nephew is a constituent of the FTSE100 (LSE:SN, NYSE:SNN).

gp.text: Gross profit was $2,196 million (H1 2025: $2,091 million), an increase of 5.0%, and the gross profit margin increased 30bps to 70.9% (H1 2025: 70.6%) as we more than offset raw materials inflation with price increases and efficiency measures in manufacturing and procurement. Operating profit increased 4.3% to $448 million (H1 2025: $429 million).

tax.text: Our reported tax for the period ended 27 June 2026 was a charge of $ 77 m, with an effective tax rate of 20.3 % (H1 2025: $ 69 m, effective tax rate of 19.1 %).

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Lease liabilities
lines.why: IFRS 16 puts every lease on the balance sheet like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.why: Obligations of uncertain timing or amount (warranties, restructuring, legal claims): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

The Group has determined that there are no critical accounting judgements and no key sources of estimation uncertainty that have a significant risk of resulting in a material adjustment to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities within the next financial year.
While such an impact can vary from year to year, these releases depend on factors which are uncertain, both as to outcome and timing.
The Group is reliant on certain key suppliers of raw materials, components, finished products and packaging materials and, in some cases, on a single supplier.

Such tariffs could increase our cost of goods sold, particularly where we rely on single-source or regionally concentrated suppliers; reduce or eliminate existing pricing advantages for certain products or geographies; require us to absorb additional costs, as our ability to pass tariff-related increases on to customers may be limited by contractual arrangements, competitive pressures, reimbursement constraints or regulatory pricing regimes; and negatively impact our gross margins, operating margins and cash flows.

The Group’s business requires continuous improvement and depends on its ability to execute business change programmes at pace and to embed continuous improvement in business-as-usual activities aligned to the RISE strategy, retaining strong governance, KPIs and metrics in order to hold management and employees to account.
The Group’s business depends on its ability to plan for and be resilient in the face of events that threaten one or more of its key locations.
Our AI technologies rely on large volumes of data, which must be accurate, current, and free of biases to yield reliable results.

The Group’s financial results depend on its ability to comply with financial reporting and disclosure requirements, comply with tax laws, appropriately manage treasury activities and avoid significant transactional errors and customer defaults.

The scope, duration and ultimate impact of tariffs and other trade measures depend on factors that are inherently uncertain and largely outside our control, including political developments, international negotiations, and actions taken by governments or supranational bodies.

The Group’s continued ability to deliver business objectives depends on its ability to hire, successfully engage and retain highly skilled talent with particular expertise and knowledge in each business unit and market in which it operates.

Implementation of environmental goals, initiatives and regulatory and reporting compliance requires increasing levels of investment and may depend on third-party performance or data that is often difficult to obtain, or is outside the control of the organisation.
